limitations: Primitive timings exclude interpreter dispatch, shared expert, residual, TP communication, and router top-k. They include alignment; all native arms also include activation quantization, assembly, and FP32 store.
Each cold sample flushes 512 MiB before the timed graph. The flush is excluded from timing; hot medians are also retained.
native-resident omits per-dispatch packing. Keeping all 75 shuffled layers duplicates 84.4 GiB per rank and is not a deployable memory plan.

Active packing reduces traffic, not the reusable allocation size (1,208,254,464 bytes for packed weights/scales). It verifies selected bytes/scales and untouched poisoned inactive experts with reversed and restored weight tables.
AITER activation quantization and BF16 accumulation introduce approximately 3.1 percent relative L2 error vs the FP32 oracle. No model-level decode quality or serving improvement is established.
The B8 packet uses MoeAlignPf/MoeGroupGluPf/MoeGroupDownPf/MoeCombinePf. These results do not qualify the different single-row decode operators.
Production dispatch and defaults are unchanged. Native MoE remains prefill-only; decode integration needs ordered TP segmentation and counter qualification.
alignment: PLOW_MOE_BENCH_DECODE=1 selects the emitted single-workgroup phase-0 alignment for both arms. The baseline separately zeroes its fixed-point accumulator; production router top-k normally performs that clear.
campaign_note: Initial four-phase alignment screens are superseded. Both captures and all arms were rerun with the matched phase-0 alignment. Preliminary raw results remain under /tmp/tp-glm53-moe-decode/four-phase.
